Grouped table with nested row and column groups

Source: R/group-table.R
phw_group_table.Rd

Turns a raw data frame (one row per record, or with a value column) into a table with a hierarchy of row groups and, optionally, of column groups. For example, counts by group (A, B, C) and then by type within each group (1, 2, 3), split into columns by year. Each group row can carry the total for its group, and you can add a total for the whole table and totals of the innermost groups across all groups. Render it with phw_flextable() or phw_reactable(): main groups are highlighted and separated with space or a rule, and the groups inside them are indented, or shifted into their own column with layout = "columns".

Usage

phw_group_table(
  data,
  rows,
  cols = NULL,
  value = NULL,
  fun = sum,
  totals = c("group", "table"),
  total_position = c("bottom", "top"),
  subtotal_position = c("header", "below"),
  col_totals = "table",
  percent = c("none", "parent", "column", "row"),
  layout = c("indent", "columns"),
  separate = c("space", "line", "both", "none"),
  highlight = TRUE,
  labels = list(),
  value_label = NULL,
  label_header = NULL,
  total_label = "Total",
  subtotal_label = "{group} total",
  missing = "Unknown",
  drop = TRUE,
  digits = 1
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

rows

Row grouping columns, outermost first, chosen as in dplyr::select(), e.g. c(group, type). Any number of levels. Strings work too.

cols

Optional column grouping columns, outermost first, e.g. year or c(year, quarter). Outer levels become headers spanning their columns.

value

Optional numeric column to summarise. Without it, rows are counted.

fun

Function applied to value within each cell. Defaults to sum (so value can hold counts of aggregated data). Use e.g. function(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE) for other statistics; group and total rows are then computed from the records in the group, not by adding up the rows below.

totals

Which row totals to show. Any of:

  • "group": each group row shows the total for its group (e.g. Group A shows the total for all of group A), at every level that has groups inside.

  • "subgroup": a block with each innermost category summed across all groups (e.g. all Type 1, all Type 2, all Type 3).

  • "table": one total row for the whole table.

Use character() or "none" for no totals.

total_position

Put the table total and the subgroup block at the "bottom" or the "top" of the table.

subtotal_position

Show group totals on the group's own heading row ("header"), or leave the heading blank and add a total row after the group ("below").

col_totals

Which column totals to show when cols is given: any of "table" (one total column) and "group" (a total column for each outermost column group, when cols has two or more levels).

percent

Add percentages to the counts: "parent" (share of the group above, e.g. Type 1 as a share of all of Group A), "column" (share of the column total), "row" (share of the row total) or "none". Only for counts and sums.

layout

"indent" puts all row labels in one column, indented by level. "columns" gives each level its own column, so each group's label sits in its own column and the groups inside it are shifted to the right.

separate

How to separate the outermost groups: "space", "line", "both" or "none".

highlight

Shade the outermost group rows?

labels

Named list of display names for the grouping columns.

value_label

Heading for the value column when there is no cols.

label_header

Heading of the label column in the "indent" layout. Defaults to the row variable labels joined with " / ".

total_label

Label for total rows and columns.

subtotal_label

Label for group totals below the group, with {group} replaced by the group name.

missing

Label for missing grouping values, or NULL to drop them.

drop

Leave out categories that have no records in a group?

digits

Decimal places for percentages and non-integer values.

Value

A phw_summary data frame. Without percent, value columns are numeric (blank group rows are NA).

Examples

set.seed(1)
dat <- data.frame(
  group = sample(c("Group A", "Group B", "Group C"), 300, TRUE),
  type = sample(c("Type 1", "Type 2", "Type 3"), 300, TRUE, prob = c(.45, .45, .1)),
  year = sample(2023:2024, 300, TRUE)
)
phw_group_table(dat, rows = c(group, type), cols = year,
                labels = list(group = "Group", type = "Type", year = "Year"))
#>  Group / Type 2023 2024 Total
#>       Group A   46   61   107
#>        Type 1   23   28    51
#>        Type 2   12   31    43
#>        Type 3   11    2    13
#>       Group B   48   53   101
#>        Type 1   16   23    39
#>        Type 2   23   25    48
#>        Type 3    9    5    14
#>       Group C   51   41    92
#>        Type 1   25   20    45
#>        Type 2   22   16    38
#>        Type 3    4    5     9
#>         Total  145  155   300

# Group totals in their own row, and totals by type across all groups
phw_group_table(dat, c(group, type), totals = c("group", "subgroup", "table"),
                subtotal_position = "below", layout = "columns")
#>          group   type   n
#>        Group A         NA
#>                Type 1  51
#>                Type 2  43
#>                Type 3  13
#>  Group A total        107
#>        Group B         NA
#>                Type 1  39
#>                Type 2  48
#>                Type 3  14
#>  Group B total        101
#>        Group C         NA
#>                Type 1  45
#>                Type 2  38
#>                Type 3   9
#>  Group C total         92
#>  Total by type         NA
#>                Type 1 135
#>                Type 2 129
#>                Type 3  36
#>          Total        300

if (requireNamespace("flextable", quietly = TRUE)) {
  phw_flextable(phw_group_table(dat, c(group, type), year, percent = "parent"))
}
